Nathaniel Day - Donor Intent and Trust Summary
DONOR INTENT (Extracted):
"To each of the towns of Lunenburg and Shirley in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, one
thousand dollars to be invested by the Selectmen or Overseers of the Poor of each of said
towns, the income derived therefrom to be used by them in improving the condition of the
worthy poor people living in and of the poor-houses in each of the said towns?
GOVERNANCE STATEMENT:
Nathaniel Day intended that the principal sum of $1,000, given to the Town of Lunenburg,
be permanently invested by the Selectmen or Overseers of the Poor. Only the income
generated from that investment is to be used, and solely to improve the condition and well-
being of the 'worthy poor, including those in the town's poorhouse.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DOCUMENT:
This document is a historical record from approximately 1901 outlining a charitable trust
established through the will of Nathaniel Day. It directs that the towns of Lunenburg and
Shirley each receive $1,000, to be invested by local officials responsible for the care of the
poor. The income is to be used exclusively to improve conditions for the 'worthy poor;'
emphasizing donor intent and long-term stewardship.

The American Legion Post 283 wishes to establish a trust fund with the town of
Lunenburg with the following conditions.
Lunenburg Trust Fund Commission to be the dispersing agency for this Trust Fund.
All funds must be used for the benefit of current or past members of American Legion
Post 283 or Lunenburg, resident Veterans.
Veterans must be eligible for membership in the American Legion.
They must be residents of the Town of Lunenburg, MA. for a minimum of 3 years.
Other dispersments may be made for qualified programs within the Town of Lunenburg
that would benefit or enhance Veteran services or programs, such as special Veterans
celebratory functions.
Funds in the amount of up to $350.00 per, any one year may be dispersed if requested.
Should the fund reach an amount in excess of $25,000.00 any amount in excess can be
used for veterans benefits. Thereafter the maximum disbursement for any one year can be
75% of that year's interest.
The intent for this is to insure that funds continue to grow so as to allow a substantial
amount can be issued to veterans.

NOTES:
• American Legion eligibility can be determined by the Town of Lunenburg
Veteran Service Officer.
Town of Lunenburg Residence can be determined by the Town Clerk.

American Legion Post 283 Trust Fund - Donor Intent Summary
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DOCUMENT:
This document is a 2013 communication from American Legion Post 283 in Lunenburg,
Massachusetts, establishing a charitable trust fund with the Town of Lunenburg. The main
theme is donor intent, specifying how funds are to be administered, who qualifies for
assistance, and how the trust should be stewarded.
DONOR INTENT LANGUAGE (Extracted for Governance Purposes - Lunenburg, MA):
• Funds must be used for the benefit of current or past members of American Legion Post
283 or Lunenburg resident veterans.
• Veterans must be eligible for American Legion membership and residents of Lunenburg
for at least 3 years.
• Disbursements may support qualified town programs that enhance veteran services or
celebratory veteran functions.
• Up to $350.00 per year may be disbursed upon request.
• If the fund exceeds $25,000.00, excess amounts may be used for veterans' benefits.
• After exceeding $25,000.00, disbursements may not exceed 75% of annual interest.
• The intent is to ensure continued growth of the fund to provide substantial long-term
support to veterans.

Article 16. To see if the town will vote to accept and forever keep and be responsible
for, the sum of $5000, the interest at four per cent, $200 a year, to be spent on the
public grounds and sidewalks within one mile of the center of the town, the said sum
being a legacy to the town under the will of Luther G. Howard and to be accepted as
a memorial to his father and mother, John Howard and Mary (Caldwell) Howard.
(Approved by finance committee.)
Voted to accept and forever keep and be responsible for, the sum of $5000 as a memorial
to John and Mary (Caldwell) Howard, the interest from said sum, at four per cent, $200
a year, to be spent on the public grounds and sidewalks within one mile of the center
of the town, the sum being a legacy to town under the will of Luther G. Howard and to
be known as the "John and Mary (Caldwell) Howard" fund.
